verdict.rationale: Pipecat's first-party interruptions docs say that on barge-in the bot stops immediately, cancels in-flight work, and readies the pipeline for new user input. That covers stopping speech and recovering the turn, and Krisp noise filtering on Pipecat Cloud reduces false interruptions. Missing for 10: documented context updating on interruption (e.g. truncating the assistant message to what was actually spoken), and independent or hands-on corroboration of barge-in behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the agent to handle interruptions (barge-in) gracefully — stopping speech, updating context, and recovering the turn

citations.quote: Interruptions (also called barge-in) let the user talk over the bot. When the user starts speaking while the bot is talking, the bot stops immediately, in-flight work is cancelled
the pipeline is ready for the new user input
Eliminates background noise and voices that cause false interruptions, powered by Krisp.
